content: Do not switch brands of interferon without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, provided it is within two days of your scheduled dose. Resume your regular dosing schedule on the usual day. Store this medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it, and avoid leaving it out of the refrigerator for more than 24 hours. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication may rarely cause or worsen serious medical conditions, including mental or mood problems (such as depression), autoimmune disorders (such as lupus or rheumatoid arthritis), blood vessel issues (such as heart disease), or infections. Close monitoring by your doctor can help reduce these risks. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience any severe symptoms or side effects. Peginterferon alfa-2a is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat chronic hepatitis B and C, which are viral infections of the liver. It works by reducing the amount of hepatitis virus in the body and enhancing the immune system's ability to fight the infection. However, it is not known if this medication can cure hepatitis B or C or prevent the transmission of the virus to others. Before using this medication, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Consult your healthcare provider for guidance on preparing and administering the medication. Inject it under the skin as directed by your doctor, typically once a week, in the abdomen or thigh. Avoid injecting near the belly button or waistline. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, lab results, and response to treatment. For a more comfortable injection, allow the medication to warm to room temperature as instructed. Do not heat it using a microwave or hot water, and do not shake the medication. Inspect the liquid for particles or discoloration before use; if present, do not use it. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose, and rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. Avoid rubbing the injection site after administration to reduce bruising. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Many individuals experience flu-like symptoms, such as headache, fatigue, fever, chills, and muscle aches, which typically subside after the first few weeks of treatment. To minimize these side effects, inject the medication at bedtime and take fever reducers or pain relievers, such as acetaminophen, before each dose. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional advice. Other possible side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dry mouth, loss of appetite, dizziness, trouble sleeping, or redness and swelling at the injection site. Tooth and gum problems may also occur, especially if dry mouth persists. Prevent dry mouth by drinking plenty of water or using a saliva substitute. Brush your teeth thoroughly at least twice daily and schedule regular dental checkups. Temporary hair loss may also occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it may cause serious mental or mood changes, which could worsen during treatment or after the last dose. It may also weaken your immune system, increasing your susceptibility to serious (and rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. Before using peginterferon alfa-2a, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, polyethylene glycol (PEG), or any other ingredients. This product may contain inactive components that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using this medication before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. This drug may cause dizziness, which can be exacerbated by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcohol consumption. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly mental or mood changes (such as severe depression or suicidal thoughts). Peginterferon alfa-2a may also slow a child’s growth, potentially resulting in a lower final adult height. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable birth control options with your healthcare provider. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as unconsciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
